papers.what_it_is: A Substack post by Javier Mancilla announcing four Kaggle datasets (SPECTRA Energy, Oil & Gas, Maintenance, Telecom) built from real industrial tables to test quantum advantage claims, and summarizing the author's Fourier Wall paper (arXiv:2607.15815).

assertions.value: The author states that four datasets, one per industry substrate, are released on Kaggle on the post's date.
assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: So today we are releasing four datasets on Kaggle, one per industry substrate
assertions.certainty_reason: The post states the release itself.

assertions.value: The author states that SPECTRA Energy holds 35,040 quarter-hour smart-meter records from a steel plant, taken from UCI 851.
assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: SPECTRA Energy, 35,040 quarter-hour smart-meter records from a steel plant, from UCI 851
assertions.certainty_reason: The post states the dataset's own makeup.

assertions.value: The author states that SPECTRA Oil & Gas holds 36,733 hourly ambient and process sensor aggregates from a gas turbine, taken from UCI 551.
assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: SPECTRA Oil & Gas, 36,733 hourly ambient and process sensor aggregates fro a gas turbine, from UCl 551.
assertions.certainty_reason: The post states the dataset's own makeup (OCR misreads UCI as UCl).

assertions.value: The author states that SPECTRA Maintenance holds 10,000 machining cycles from the AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset, UCI 601.
assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: SPECTRA Maintenance, 10,000 machining cycles from the AI4I 2020 predictive maintenance dataset, UCI 601.
assertions.certainty_reason: The post states the dataset's own makeup.

assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: SPECTRA Telecom, 3,150 telecom customers from the Iranian Churn dataset, 563.
assertions.certainty_reason: The post states the dataset's own makeup (the 563 is the UCI id as printed).

assertions.value: The author states that all four substrates are real, popular, CC BY 4.0 public tables with DOIs, that the releases are CC BY 4.0 derivatives, and that both the original and the release should be cited.

both the original and the release should be cited.

assertions.value: The author states that the covariates are real throughout and that nothing is synthesised on the feature side.
assertions.anchor: What is real and what is not, p.5, OCR
quotes: The covariates are real throughout. Nothing is synthesised on the feature side.
assertions.certainty_reason: The post states the scope of what is real in its own release.

assertions.value: The author states that the leading genuine fields are re-expressed as continuous periodic phases on the interval from minus pi to pi, the representation in which cyclic structure survives.
assertions.anchor: What is real and what is not, p.5, OCR
quotes: leading genuine fields are additionally re-expressed as continuous periodic phases the interval from minus pi to pi, which is the representation where cyclic structure survives.
assertions.certainty_reason: The post states how its own release is built.

assertions.value: The author reports that in the Fourier Wall paper, feeding the same models variance-maximizing PCA components instead of periodic phases collapses every lane to near chance.
assertions.anchor: What is real and what is not, p.5, OCR
quotes: feeding the same models with variance- maximizing PCA components instead of periodic phases collapses every lane to nea
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper; no numbers or setup are given in the post.

assertions.value: The author reports that with phase features the quantum lane reaches 0.752 and trees reach 0.724, a gap of +0.217 on representation alone.
assertions.anchor: What is real and what is not, p.5, OCR
quotes: phase features reach 0.752 for the quantum lane and 0.724 for trees.
gap of +0.217 on representation alone.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper, with no setup given here.
assertions.reader_inference: The +0.217 gap is stated by the author as a representation effect (phases against PCA), not as the 0.752 minus 0.724 difference.

assertions.value: The author states that part of the released label is synthetic: inside one behaviorally defined segment, the label additionally reflects an operationally plausible automated campaign.

Inside one behaviorally defined segment, the released label additionally reflects an operationally plausible automated campaign

assertions.value: The author states that the construction details, the generating parameters and the answer key are retained privately, and that the full specification can be shared with reviewers on request.
assertions.anchor: What is real and what is not, p.6, OCR

full specification can be shared with reviewers on request.

assertions.reader_inference: The answer key and generator are not public, so the synthetic label cannot be checked independently.

assertions.value: The author asks quantum-circuit users to beat a complete bar: trained-frequency GAM, trained-frequency GA2M, gradient-boosted trees, logistic regression, and the order-matched joint twin, all on identical splits with paired confidence bounds on held-out rows.
assertions.anchor: What we would like people to do with them, p.6, OCR
quotes: whether you beat a complete bar: trained-frequency GAM, trained-frequency GA2M, gradient-boosted trees, logistic regression, and the order matched joint twin that most advantage claims omit.
on identica splits, with paired confidence bounds on held-out rows.
assertions.certainty_reason: The post defines the baseline set it asks users to report.

assertions.value: The author reports that in the paper, raising the joint twin's term budget from 6 to 20, or its interaction order to 4, moved it between 0.577 and 0.595 on the dense substrate.
assertions.anchor: What we would like people to do with them, p.6, OCR
quotes: raisi the joint twin's term budget from 6 to 20, or its interaction order to 4, moved it between 0.577 and 0.595 on the dense substrate.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper.

assertions.value: The author states that the spectrum on the dense substrate was dense, not under-enumerated.
assertions.anchor: What we would like people to do with them, p.6, OCR
quotes: The spectrum was dense, not und enumerated.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's interpretation of the twin-budget result.

assertions.certainty_reason: A vendor describing its own product's status.

assertions.value: The author states a common pattern: someone runs a gradient-boosted tree with default parameters and beats the variational quantum model by a margin that no amount of ansatz engineering closes.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, p.2, OCR
quotes: boosted tree with default parameters and beats you by a margin that no amount of ansatz engineering closes.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's general statement with no data in the post.

assertions.value: The author states that the paper The Fourier Wall (arXiv:2607.15815) claims the quantum-advantage contests were unwinnable before the first qubit was allocated, a property of the datasets rather than of the models.
assertions.anchor: Introduction, p.2, OCR
quotes: The Fourier Wall (arXiv:2607.15815)
is a property of the datasets rather than of the models.
assertions.certainty_reason: A summary of the author's other paper.

assertions.value: The author states that an angle-encoded variational quantum model is a partial Fourier series in its inputs, and that the accessible frequency set is fixed by the data-encoding gates, not by the variational ansatz.
assertions.anchor: The short version of the argument, p.2, OCR
quotes: An angle-encoded variational quantum model is a partial Fourier series in its inputs
accessible frequency set is fixed by the data-encoding gates, not by the variational ansatz.
assertions.certainty_reason: A structural statement given without proof in the post; the proof is in the cited paper.

assertions.value: The author states that gradient-boosted trees capture low-frequency structure of any interaction order, given enough splits.
assertions.anchor: The short version of the argument, p.2, OCR
quotes: Gradient- boosted trees capture low-frequency structure of any interaction order, given enou splits.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement from the author's other paper, with no proof in the post.

assertions.value: The author states that additive models capture per-feature structure and pairwise-interaction models capture order-2 structure.
assertions.anchor: The short version of the argument, p.2, OCR
quotes: Additive models capture per- feature structure.
Pairwise-interaction models capture order-2 structure.
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement from the author's other paper, with no proof in the post.

assertions.value: The author states that a quantum model can only earn a genuine edge where all classical reaches end at the same time, an intersection that requires five conditions at once: the target's spectrum off the integer grid, a dominant interaction of order 3 or higher, near-independent encoded features, a joint coordinate that oscillates fast enough, and a joint spectrum dense beyond enumeration.
assertions.anchor: The short version of the argument, p.2, OCR
quotes: That intersection requires five conditions to hold simultaneously
The target's spectrum sits off the integer grid.
The dominant interaction is genuinely joint, of order 3 or higher.
The encoded features are near-independent
The joint spectrum is dense beyond enumeration.
assertions.certainty_reason: A summary of the author's other paper; no proof or conditions' formal statement is given in the post.

assertions.value: The author reports that on a controlled substrate in the paper, a classical bar without an order-matched twin credits the quantum model with an advantage at 0.758, and adding the twin gives a classical read of the same structure at 0.968.
assertions.anchor: The short version of the argument, p.3, OCR
quotes: a classical bar without an order- matched twin credits the quantum model with an advantage at 0.758.
Add the twin, which costs about a second of fitting, and the same structure is read classically at 0.968.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper; the metric is not named in the post.

assertions.value: The author states that public tabular exports essentially never satisfy the five conditions at once, which the author calls the wall.
assertions.anchor: The short version of the argument, p.3, OCR
quotes: Public tabular exports essentially never satisfy the five conditions at once.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim; no survey is given in the post.

assertions.value: The author reports that on real industrial smart-meter data with the real peak-load target, gradient-boosted trees reach a held-out ROC-AUC of 0.999 and SPECTRA returns refuse.
assertions.anchor: The certificate has to be able to say no, p.3, OCR
quotes: the real peak-load target, gradient-boosted trees reach a held-out ROC-AUC
0.999 and SPECTRA returns refuse.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper, by the product's vendor.

assertions.value: The author reports that on the same real energy phases, carrying the label of an interacting quantum process, the dynamics-matched quantum model reaches 0.994 against a complete classical bar that tops out at 0.699.
assertions.anchor: The certificate has to be able to say no, p.3, OCR
quotes: the dynamics-matched quantum model reaches 0.994 against a complete classical bar that tops out at 0.699.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper, by the product's vendor; the label is partly synthetic.
assertions.reader_inference: The label here belongs to a simulated interacting process on real phases, not to a real-world outcome.

assertions.value: The author reports that clamping the interaction coupling to zero collapses the quantum model to chance, a gap of +0.484.
assertions.anchor: The certificate has to be able to say no, p.3, OCR
quotes: Clamp the interaction coupli to zero and it collapses to chance, a gap of +0.484.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper.

assertions.value: The author states, as a caveat, that at seven sites the exact classical simulator of the same process family ties the accuracy at 0.993.
assertions.anchor: The certificate has to be able to say no, p.3, OCR
quotes: At seven sites, the exact classical simulator of the same process family ties the accuracy at 0.993, as it must.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper; a caveat that limits the accuracy result.
assertions.reader_inference: At this size the 0.994 accuracy shows no accuracy advantage over exact classical simulation.

assertions.value: The author reports that the measured classical per-sample cost grows as two to the power 1.14 n (printed 2^1.14n), with n the number of sites.
assertions.anchor: The certificate has to be able to say no, p.3, OCR
quotes: the measured classical per-sample cost grows as 2^1.14n
assertions.certainty_reason: A result reported from the author's other paper.

assertions.value: The author states that the wall-clock crossover against a quantum processor lands at roughly 13 to 19 sites.
assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: against a quantum processor lands at roughly 13 to 19 sites.

assertions.value: The author states that the certified benefit is resource separation, not an accuracy miracle.
assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: The certified benefit is resource separation, not an accuracy miracle.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's conclusion.

assertions.value: The author states that every public benchmark is, by the paper's own diagnosis, on the classical side of the wall, so a claim about where quantum advantage lives cannot be tested on them.
assertions.anchor: The gap this release fills, p.4, OCR
quotes: Every public benchmark is, by the paper's own diagnosis, on the classical side.
You cannot test a claim about where quantum advantage lives on data that structurally cannot host it.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author's claim resting on the author's own diagnosis.

assertions.value: The author states that the negative benchmark literature is evidence about datasets, and repeating it produces no new information.
